summary: Rollback-induced pin loss routes tenant to degraded fallback variant during staged canary
description:
Issue summary:
A staged canary rollback of orchestrator control-plane snapshots caused a short-lived metadata epoch rollback. During the rollback window, tenant pin anchors for model selection were observed to expire or be invalidated and traffic for a single NimbusHealth tenant was routed to a degraded fallback variant.

Impact:
- Customer-facing quality degradations on ~2.1k requests over a 13-minute window (response mismatches, tokenization deltas).
- Billing spike: fallback to a larger variant increased token cost by ~2.8x for affected requests.
- Customer reported streaming disconnects for several sessions; one SLO breach for latency observed.

Environment:
- Prod us-east, Redwood hosted API, dedicated tenant on enterprise plan (NimbusHealth).
- Canary rollout for orchestrator v2.13.1 -> v2.13.2 with staged weight shift.

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) Canary weight ramp initiated at 2025-03-07T14:03:00Z.
2) Control plane attempted to commit a condensed snapshot; commit failed and orchestrator performed a rollback to epoch 5421->5419 at 2025-03-07T14:07:44Z.
3) During rollback window (14:07:44Z - 14:20:55Z) routing-mesh accepted requests using a mixture of snapshot fingerprints. Pin anchor TTLs (configured 10m) were re-evaluated against the older epoch and several anchors resolved as expired.
4) Requests for tenant nimbus-prod-17 were routed to fallback variant open-llm-ggml-13b (degraded quality) instead of tenant-pinned redwood-rlhf-7b.

Observed behavior:
- Tenant-level pin token present in request headers, but routing returned variant: open-llm-ggml-13b.
- Edge and serving logs show successful pin lookup but a mismatch on metadata-hash check against snapshot epoch.
- Billing metrics show an increased cost during the window due to larger per-request compute footprint on fallback variant.

Expected behavior:
- Rollback should not invalidate existing tenant pins or should honor pin lifetime across metadata epoch transitions; routing should prefer pinned variant or serve a graceful degraded response with preserved cost profile.

Logs/Telemetry pointers:
- Orchestrator snapshot events: https://console.redwood.example/logs?query=orchestrator+snapshot+5421
- Routing-mesh traces: trace-id list attached in investigation notes.
- Billing spike chart: /console/costs/tenant/nimbus-prod-17?from=2025-03-07T14:00Z&to=2025-03-07T15:00Z

Initial customer report:
- NimbusHealth CS rep reported quality regressions and unexpected cost increase at 2025-03-07T14:25Z via support email. The customer provided one sample request/response pair showing different model outputs for the same session token across two close timestamps.

Investigation summary (high level):
- Hypothesis: orchestrator rollback created a transient metadata-epoch mismatch between edge and routing-mesh; routing-mesh performs an epoch-bound validation step before honoring pin anchors. When validation failed against the rolled-back epoch, the pin was treated as stale and routing fell back to compatibility-based variant selection.
- Evidence: control-plane commit/rollback logs show snapshot reversion at 14:07:44Z. Edge logs around 14:08:00Z show pin-lookup returned anchor against snapshot 5421 but routing decision used snapshot 5419 metadata-hash, causing TTL re-evaluation.
- Related: Similar behavior previously traced in SUP-210945 (snapshot merge retains old routing).

Temporary customer-facing status message sent: "We are investigating unexpected model selection behavior for a small set of requests during a scheduled canary activity. Impact is isolated; we will provide a remediation within the hour."

investigation_notes:
Detailed findings:
- Root cause appears to be orchestration of snapshot application across control-plane and data-plane services. During rollback the routing-mesh validated pin anchors against an epoch-local fingerprint, invalidated anchors that did not match, and triggered fallback-path selection.
- TTL semantics: pin TTL is set relative to anchor creation epoch; when anchor re-validation sees a lower epoch, code treats anchor as expired instead of carrying forward. This is the logic gap.
- Edge-case: if rollback window overlaps with active sessions whose anchors are near TTL boundary (within ~2m) they are disproportionately affected.
- Reproduction steps developed for staging and confirmed with synthetic traffic using the canary harness. See synthetic run logs: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/9865/replay
workaround: Immediate workaround executed: 1) Ran targeted pin-reconciliation for nimbus-prod-17 to re-anchor sessions to the expected model. 2) Temporarily lowered metadata refresh TTL on routing-mesh and edge from 2m -> 30s to reduce stale fingerprint acceptance during orchestration operations. 3) Disabled automatic fallback to variant selection on metadata-hash mismatch for enterprise customers for the duration of the immediate mitigation window.
resolution: Mitigation completed and validated. A permanent fix is under review: change pin-validation logic to allow epoch-tolerant rebind for anchors younger than configured TTL and add atomic snapshot handoff to avoid rollback-induced mismatches. Customer billing review requested; finance will propose a credit for the affected window. Ticket remains open for PR and postmortem.
